raw_comment: The first thing that stuck out to me is the instability of the graph. The average game duration has not increased or decreased steadily over time, and instead has altered variously. Another thing that I noticed was that baseball games were at an all time high just a few years ago. I wonder why this is because I would think games would be longer in earlier years. I also wonder what made baseball games so short before. Back in the 80s, games were around the same length they are today. This relates to my community and I because I am a baseball fan. I also have friends and family that are baseball fans. The duration of the game plays a large role in how you enjoy the game. However, I believe this depends on whether you are at the game or not. When you are at the game, it is easier to enjoy a longer game when you are there, but on TV, longer games can get boring. In this graph, the average duration of an MLB game over the years is shown. A catchy headline to apply to this graph is, Shifting rules to shift time.

The duration of each game seems to increase as the years progress, with exception of somewhere in the 2000’s where time decreased. 2022 was the pinnacle, measuring the longest game at 3 hours and 8 minutes. Right after 2022, the duration of a game significantly dropped to 2 hours and 39 minutes.
One of the biggest things that I wonder is what caused the length of time to suddenly decrease in 2023 and why it was caused.
This relates to my community because some of my friends and family members watch baseball. 
Catchy headline: Baseball Incentives

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that the average game duration was increasing from the time of 1980 to 2022. However, even though the duration was increasing, there were some dips, or sudden decreases during this period. I also notice  that ironically, now in 2023, the average game duration is nearly the same rate as it was back in 1980. 

2. I wonder why the line on the graph have sudden drops. I’m not too familiar with the game of baseball, so I’m curious whether or not there were rule changes that were present before this year. If there were small changes that occurred to, for example, the time limit of pitchers, in recent years before 2023, could that be the reason of the sudden drops. I also wonder if since the game duration for this year has decreased, will the annual ticket sells go up.

3. This relates to my community because many of my friends enjoy watching baseball. On top of that, our high school has a baseball team. It’s possible that the rules for our league could possibly change as well.

4. This graph is showing the average game duration for the first 3 weeks of MLB games from the year 1980-present.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?

I notice that the data show an overall increase in average game duration from 1980 to 2022. I also notice that there are occasionally "dips" in the data. On a related note, I notice that for every decade the end of the decade's average game duration is greater than the start of the decade's. However, I think that it's worth noting that the difference between the average game duration in 2000 and the average game duration in 2010 is relatively small. Ignoring the dip in average game duration in 2023, there is a pretty big dip in the early- to mid-2000s.

2. What do you wonder?

I wonder why average game durations had been increasing from 1980 to 2022. I wonder why there are the occasional dips in the data. I especially wonder about the early- to mid-2000s dip; the 2000-2010 decade is not like the other decades, where there is such a large and prolonged dip.

3. How does this relate to you and your community?

N/a

4. What's going on in this graph?

Major League Baseball Returns Average Game Durations to Their 1980s Times

raw_comment:
1. I note that game time for baseball rose the greatest between 1985 and 1995 in this graph. Between the 2000s and 2005, game duration gradually decreased before increasing dramatically after that year. It peaked about 2020, with games lasting significantly longer than three hours. After 2020, the game's time reduced steadily, eventually reaching almost 3 hours.

2.  I'm curious why this drop is so significant. I expected that a timed pitch clock would shorten the game, but I had no clue by how much. I believe pitchers are suddenly concerned with pitching within the allotted time frame, and they are throwing much earlier than they would usually, even though there is still plenty of time on the pitch clock. They may sense the pressure of a time constraint and pitch earlier than they would usually. But I'm not sure if this is true for most pitchers these days, or just a subset of them.

3. This relates to my community because I come from a city where baseball is a prominent sport. I wonder how enjoyers of baseball will react to the average increase of baseball games just to suddenly drop in the current year.

4. "How Will New Game-Shifting Rules Change the MLB Forever"

raw_comment:
I notice that within one year, the game duration of baseball has dropped drastically by almost half an hour. 
At first, I wondered why the time decreased so much until I read that they added a pitching clock that limited the time which would have decreased the amount of time spent. Then I wondered, how this affect the audience watching the game and those playing in it as well. 
This relates to my community as I find nowadays people have shortened attention spans for a lot of things, including scrolling through 15-second videos. These shortened baseball games have a direct impact on my community as it enforced the idea of things getting too long to pay attention to. 
Strike! Your time is out.

raw_comment:
This graph shows an overall increase in the duration of MLB baseball games throughout the year, with the duration peaking relatively recently. However, the average duration of games at the start of the 2023 season dropped dramatically when compared to the 2022 season and appears to now be around the same duration of games in the 1980s. 

I wonder how these new rules were decided, and how they were able to bring major results almost immediately. With most things, it can take a while for the effects of changes to be noticeable, but that is not the case with the duration of MLB games. 

I am not much of a baseball fan, though I have been dragged to quite a few games in my life, and my dad enjoys watching them on television. I think the changes to the duration of games will be helpful for people like me who don't care much about the game and get annoyed when it drags on for hours. 

Title: "In the Newest Season, Three-Hour MLB Games have Struck Out"

raw_comment:
The graph shows an overall increasing trend between 1980 and 2020, meaning an increase in the average MLB baseball game. The highest peak was shortly before 2022, around 3 hours and 8 minutes. However, between 2022 and 2023, there is a significant drop, essentially to 1980 levels. Almost 40 years of growth is undone in 1 year.
I wonder how the die-hard baseball fans felt about such a switch, as that was a very big change in a short amount of time. Im also curious if in the following years, well see similar increasing patterns as the 1980s to 2020s saw. 
What happens in the major leagues tends to trickle down, so perhaps we'll see changes in college baseball games as well. Personally, Im down with the shorter games. As someone who has been to several baseball games, I agree they were too long. 

Title: New Rules, New Playing Field

raw_comment:
Thanks to all the students who responded.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  “A New Meaning to 'Fastball'” by Sami of Saint Thomas Aquinas High School in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; “Fast Ball: How Has the New Rule Changes Affected the Pace of the Game” by Vivi of Eden Prairie High School in Minnesota; "New Rules, Shorter Games, MLB Makes a Change!" by Grace and "Does 2023 Mark The End of Long Baseball Games?" by Jayna, both from Perth Amboy High School in New Jersey; and, "From Slowball to Fastball: How Baseball Games are Speeding Up" by Adam, “Heating Up: MLB Throws a Curveball with New Fast-Paced Games” by Dillon and “Baseball: America’s Pastime is Catching up to Speed” by Edy, all three from of California Polytechnic San Luis Obispo.
 
This is the last graph of the school year.  Looking forward to your returning and a new crop of graphs in early September.
 
Signing off – Sharon Hessney from Boston, who loves the relaxed baseball pastime but is looking forward to the excitement of a faster game, and Christine Franklin, American Statistical Association Statistical K-12 Ambassador and University of Georgia Emerita statistics faculty from Athens, Georgia, who LOVES attending and scoring baseballs games regardless of the length of the game.

raw_comment:
1. I note that game time for baseball rose the greatest between 1985 and 1995 in this graph. Between the 2000s and 2005, game duration gradually decreased before increasing dramatically after that year. It peaked about 2020, with games lasting significantly longer than three hours. After 2020, the game's time reduced steadily, eventually reaching almost 3 hours.

2.  I'm curious why this drop is so significant. I expected that a timed pitch clock would shorten the game, but I had no clue by how much. I believe pitchers are suddenly concerned with pitching within the allotted time frame, and they are throwing much earlier than they would usually, even though there is still plenty of time on the pitch clock. They may sense the pressure of a time constraint and pitch earlier than they would usually. But I'm not sure if this is true for most pitchers these days, or just a subset of them.

3. This relates to my community because I come from a city where baseball is a prominent sport. I wonder how enjoyers of baseball will react to the average increase of baseball games just to suddenly drop in the current year.

4. "How Will New Game-Shifting Rules Change the MLB Forever"

raw_comment: This graph demonstrates the evolution of the average duration of Major League Baseball games.  This graph was created in response to the league creating new rules to speed up the game, including a pitch clock, a limit on pickoff throws by the pitcher, and eliminating the shift.  The main thing that stands out from the graph is the largest decline in time which happened between 2022 and 2023.  This is most likely a direct result of the new rules to shorten the game.  For a majority of the years displayed on the graph, the average duration is between 2 hours and 45 minus and 3 hours.  It is also clear that in the last 10 years the games have been much longer, mostly over 3 hours.  Another thing that stands out is in 1980s, the games were even shorter than they are now.  I wonder why this occurred.  Was there less strategy 40 years ago?  Was there a pitch clock that was eliminated?  Did they have shorter innings due to less hitting?  This graph is relevant to me and my community because like myself, very few baseball fans could stand the amount of time the pitcher would take to throw the ball.  This makes the game far more captivating and will potentially draw in more viewers.  I would entitle this graph: "Less Time is Better in Baseball."

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that in 2022 the games would last longer however since they introduced the pitch clock games length have taken a huge plunge. Went from about 3 hours to 2 hrs and 30 min that's almost a 40 min difference. This huge plunge is shocking but games used to be this length back in the 80s. Without the rules, each plate appearance besides strikeouts takes more pitches than 30 years ago which explains why the games would take so long.

2. I wonder how fans feel about this change. The main idea was of them to attract younger fans. Will they lose older fans with this though? People who have been loving the game since childhood have been taking the news with mixed feelings. Some prefer shorter games and some feel as though shorter games should mean lower prices for tickets. 

3. I come from a predominantly Hispanic community. One thing we love is baseball. This change has had mixed feelings in my community too. Older people are not liking the fact they aren't getting a run for their money while younger people are happy that it's more exciting at a faster pace. I am personally not the biggest baseball fan however I went to see the Yankees and I did prefer the faster pace game. It kept it interesting for me.

4. MLB New Rules Changed Baseball Forever

raw_comment:
1. I discovered that an MLB game in 2023 will last as long as one from the 1980s. There was a noticeable rising trend in the average duration between the two time periods up until 2023. This graph's greatest fall, which occurred between 2022 and 2023, suggests that those years saw the implementation of the strictest new laws. The average game time was reduced to 2 hours and 39 minutes, a decrease of around 30 minutes.
2. I wonder what prompted the MLB to implement these new rules. Could implementing these new regulations make the game more interesting for baseball fans? Could the reason as to why games took longer be due to the lack of technology to review invalid plays? Could this have caused baseball fans from before to lose interest in the sport?
3. This relates to me and my community because baseball is one of the most popular sports so when it develops, I'm curious how competitions at the middle and high school levels will change. Also, it is now known that technology has taken over the entire world and how this could affect how people watch. Younger generations in particular have spent our entire lives viewing brief video clips and parts and haven't really had the attention span to sit through a 3-hour movie, much less a sporting event. It could be argued that shorter sporting events prevent viewers from getting bored and turning away because of the rising rates of indifference and impatience.
4. A Curveball Into Time!

raw_comment:
1) I notice that in the last 4 decades, the average time for baseball games has increased of a total 30 minutes. However, that rapidly declined in 2022, making the average time to go to 2 hours and 39 minutes. To go into more detail, the lowest record has been around 2 hours and 46 minutes in 2008. Until 2023, where we see a huge decrease in time, which is a 29 minute difference (3:08 -> 2:39). Also, I notice that the time for 2023 (2:39) is close to the starting average in 1980 (a bit over 2:30). 

I wonder what caused the duration time to start increasing over the years and why they just decided to make the rule. Also, I wonder how this rule will affect the games' time over the years. What would cause the games' time to increase, the weather? the players? injuries? 

This relates to my community because many are fans of baseball, either going to the games or watching from home. These times may affect how many people attend/watch because if the games are shorter more people may go. 

A Swing in a New Direction

raw_comment:
Evan Morgans, Strath Haven High School

What do you notice? 
- I notice that the reduction of the game is about 29 minutes, which is quite a large amount of time taken from a sports game, especially baseball. I understand this change is meant to engage more people to watch games and to make the games more competitive, along with the addition of the other rules, though these changes don't seem necessary. Fielders are no longer allowed to adjust to certain batters, which feels like a nitpick more than a crucial change to the game. Most of these changes feel like exactly that, a nitpick to gain more revenue. 
What do you wonder?
- I wonder if these changes actually helped generate more viewers for games and if the games this season are actually "more competitive". 
Impact on community
- There's not much impact, since watching baseball is purely entertainment. Though to the baseball community, it's quite a big impact with generally mixed reviews. For regular viewers, this is only a negative since they would have already had the time to take to watch MLB games. Though now it's shorter, and they're missing a lot more of what they love about the sport, almost 30 minutes worth of time. Though for casual watchers who'll watch once in a while with family, this is a welcome change. They usually don't care enough to spend 3 hours of time to watch, so now when they decide to watch they have almost 30 minutes saved out of their day. 
Title
- Length of baseball games over the years

raw_comment:
1. I notice that there have been a number of 'peaks' where game duration has increased significantly, then decreased again, before repeating the cycle. I also observe that the length of the games this fall is the shortest since the 1980s. The largest single-year divergence and outlier in an otherwise somewhat constant pattern is the decline between 2022 and 2023. 

2. I'm curious as to why the time decreased so noticeably between 2022 and 2023 and why times always seem to creep back up after time decreases. I also wonder how the expectations and enjoyment of watching contemporary baseball games have changed over time. 

3. Baseball is one of the most popular sports in my area, so when it develops, I'm curious how competitions at the middle and high school levels will change. How would a lower-income city like mine be impacted by technology that our schools might not be able to buy if PitchCom technology spreads to even minor league games? One of the most well-liked sports in my area may radically change as a result of these queries.

raw_comment:
What do I notice? 
- The new rules appear to be in direct response to the recent seasons' (around 2020 and after) game lengths, since those are the ones where the time peaked at a little under 3 hours and 15 minutes. 
- One of the new rules this season includes a pitching timer, and that appears to be having a major effect on decreasing the time of the games (from around 3 hours to only 2 hours and 40 minutes). 
- The average time of games this season seem to be returning back to the average times of games around the 1980s. 
What do I wonder? 
- How much have the different rules decreased time this season individually? 
- How will this data look more towards the post-season? Will the time increase due to being closer to the World Series, or will it continue to decrease as a result of the new rules?
What do I think is going on in this graph? 
This graph is displaying the average game times in the MLB from 1980 to this current season? 
How does this relate to you and your community? 
- A few weeks ago my family and I went to a Yankees game, and we noticed that the game was significantly shorter than games we had gone to in the past. Usually, a game would take up an entire day almost (including getting to and from the stadium). However, we were able to get in and out of the stadium in only around 4 or 5 hours. Throughout the game, we felt that the pitching timer had the largest impact on the duration.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

I first noticed that from 1980 to 2022, the average game duration during Major League Baseball games has increased from around two hours and thirty minutes to three hours and eight minutes. However, after 2022 when the new rules were put into place, the average game duration has decreased almost back to the same amount it was in 1980 I also noticed the line from 2022 to 2023 is yellow which could be because the main objective of the text that goes along with it is to look at how the implementation of new rules has affected game time.

What do you wonder? 

How do commercial breaks and pitching changes affect the length of a baseball game? What are the implications of longer game durations on broadcasting and advertising revenue for the league? What factors contributed to the large increase in game duration of Major League Baseball from 1980 to 2022?

How does this relate to you and your community?

The increasing game duration of Major League Baseball relates to my community and I because although I don’t regularly watch baseball, it’s popular with the people around me. If games were to continue being regularly three hours, it could make fans lose interest in watching through the whole game since hardly anyone wants to watch the same thing for three hours straight.

raw_comment:
-I've noticed that the average game time has been shifting since the 1980s, increasing till 2023. The lowest it has ever gone since the 1980s was roughly 2 hours and 46 minutes in 2008. From 2022 to 2023, there was a significant linear reduction from an average of 3 hours and 8 months to 2 hours and 39 minutes, a difference of over 29 minutes. The games were the longest ever during the pandemic, most likely due to all of the health standards that had to be followed. 

-I'm curious as to why the dramatic reduction occurred in 2022. I'm also curious about whether baseball will become a more efficient and popular sport. I'm especially curious how engaged or disinterested individuals have gotten in the sport as a result of the new scheduling. Are pitch clocks reducing player performance? 

-This does not directly affect me, but it does affect some of the individuals in my community. Many adults in my town aspire to play in the Major League Baseball, and with fewer opportunities to do so, they will have to start training harder. In addition, I've been wanting to witness a basketball game, and the fact that it's shorter in length will make the experience more pleasurable.

-Are MLB games becoming speedless or worthless?

raw_comment:
1. From 1980 to 2022, I saw a gradual increase in the average game duration. Over the past few years, the games have progressively lasted longer. The average game length was reset to the 1980 average time in 2023. The average game time was cut back by about 30 minutes, to 2 hours and 39 minutes.

2. I'm curious as to how the games were playing more slowly. Could the weather, the players, the rules, or even the year have an impact on the game. Not to add that it's intriguing to note how the new regulation cut the length of new games by approximately 30 minutes. 

3. Given that many people in my town enjoy sports, this is relevant to me. Some people watch them live, while others who operate from a screen. The majority of those who watch MLB games live will be impacted by this rule. They no longer have to wait as long to enjoy the game thanks to the new rule.

I saw that the length of an MLB game in 2023 is comparable to that of an MLB game in the 1980s. time.

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that there is a slow increase in the average game duration from 1980 to 2022. The games were slowly running longer over the past years. In 2023, the average game duration was taken back to the average time from 1980. The average game duration was shortened down back to 2 hours and 39 minutes, nearly 30 minutes shorter.

2. I wonder how the games were leisurely taking longer. Could the game be affected by the climate, players, rules or even the year. Not to mention the new rule is interesting to see how it made new games nearly 30 minutes shorter. 

3. This relates to my community because sports are enjoyed by many. There are those who watch them in person and others that do so from a screen. This rule mainly affects the fans who see the MLB games in person. With the new rule, they have to wait less and are able to enjoy the game more easily.

4. The Swing That Turned the Times.

1. I seemed to have noticed the obvious and most drastic decrease in game duration between 2022 and 2023 seasons. And before the rule change, the game duration was 30 minutes longer since 1980 due to there being many more televised games in the modern day. Which tends to take much longer than non-televised games. 

2. I wonder what new rules were being applied and do they specifically target the decrease in time for game duration. Along with lowering the points required or just to mainly reduce the time.

3. This relates to me and my community since MLB games are very enjoyable to watch but at the same time it feels very slow making it boring for the fans to watch. Compared to other sports like basketball and football they are almost just as long but they have great impactful moments that move the crowd. If they lowered the time to watch MLB games then it would be more enjoyable to watch.

4. MLB Makes A Change!

raw_comment:
I notice that there have been multiple 'peaks' in which game time increases by a dramatic amount, then falls again, only to repeat the cycle. I also notice that this fall is the shortest games have been since the 80s. The fall between 2022 and 2023 is the largest single-year difference and is an outlier in an otherwise semi-consistent pattern. 

I wonder why the time dropped so dramatically between 2022 and 2023, and what is causing times to seemingly creep back up after time drops. I also wonder how these changes in time affect the expectations and viewing experience of modern baseball games. 

In my community, baseball is one of the most popular sports, and as it changes, I wonder how games at the middle and high school levels will evolve. If technology like PitchCom becomes widespread in even the minor league games, how will a lower-income city like my own be affected by technology our schools may not be able to afford? These questions can completely change one of the most popular sports in my community.

The final inning: game times dropping in response to a record high.

raw_comment:
What I notice in this graph is that you can observe a steady increase in the duration of the baseball games from 1980 to 2020, with multiple peaks between the 1990s and 2000s. The average duration time hits its peak during 2020 before severely declining in 2022. I can also notice between 1990 and 2010, the average game duration time mostly stayed between  2 hours and 45 minutes to 3 hours.

I wonder if the effects and aftermath of COVID had something to do with the decline in game duration time since severe protocols were probably put in place. I also wonder if the new generation of baseball players affected how the games play out during the seasons making them shorter or their play decisions. Could this also do with the advertisements being broadcasted on live TV or the attention span of the audience as baseball evolved over time?

This relates to my community because it has been known that technology has taken over the whole world. Specifically with the younger generations, we are grown up watching short clips of videos and segments and never really had the attention span to sit through a 3-hour movie, much less a sports game. It could be said that the growing rate of inattention and impatience has led to the sports games being shorter so the watcher doesn't have the opportunity to be bored and keep watching.

My headline would be, "Pack Up Your Peanuts, Baseball Games Are Declining In Watch Time"

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 

I saw that the time between 2022 and 2023 was significantly shorter. It went from 3 hours and 8 minutes to 2 hours and 39 minutes.  A baseball game has never lasted longer than around 3 hours and 10 minutes. Additionally, I observed that the current time is very comparable to the lowest point in 1980.

What do you wonder?

I'm curious as to why game play duration has gotten longer over time. I wonder whether any rules from 1980 were perhaps added again to make games last less time. I'm curious about how others feel about this as well, do they desire longer games or are they pleased with the current length of time?

How does this relate to you and your community?

This is relevant to me and my community since, as a result of living in a Hispanic town, many people there watch or play baseball. Here, baseball is a very well-liked sport. 

What's going on in this graph? 

"Three Strikes and Hurry Out!"

Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  This is our last release of this school year.  
Today’s graph shows the average “speed” of major league baseball games since 1980 for the first three weeks of each season.  New rules were instituted this season that include a clock to require pitchers and hitter to “play ball” with shorter delays, no more shifting players into the infield to make outs and making it easier to steal bases.  Is baseball going to get faster and more entertaining?  Could it be as exciting as its sport competitors – football, basketball and hockey?  Will in person and broadcasted audiences increase in size?
From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online for the four questions.  We have added a suggestion to the “What do you notice?” question.  If your notice includes a claim, please back it up with evidence that supports your claim.  
By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the free link to the online article that included these graphs.  

You can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

This is the last graph of the school year.  “See” you in early September.

raw_comment:
First time in a little less than 40 years that the average game duration is lower than 2 hours and 45 minutes. Since 1980 this current year is the lowest three opening week game time duration. Scoring will be increases as less time is given to the pitcher giving more time for the player at bat to get hits causing more high scoring games. So this would directly lead to more points on the end score. This may lead to more people attending the game with action happening almost every other pitch will have people out their seats lowering the actually game duration as well.

How will this affect the speed of the game?

raw_comment:
I observed a significant decline in the average duration of baseball games between 2022 and 2023. Since 1980, the typical game has lasted over three hours, with a peak in the mid-1990s to mid-2010s and a minor decrease in the mid-2000s. This reduction may have been due to certain rule modifications during that period. The sharpest decline occurred in 2022-2023, likely a result of the pitch clock and the introduction of transmitters for pitchers and catchers, which minimized delays. 

I wonder how this change has affected ratings, and what the relationship between time and viewership is. 

I watch baseball sometimes and this makes it less of a time commitment so sit down and watch a game for almost 4 hours. 

Baseball Makes a Change!

raw_comment:
I noticed that there was a sharp decrease in game duration between the 2022 and 2023 seasons. I also noticed that before the rule change, game duration had increased by about 30 minutes since 1980. Because there are many more televised games in the modern day, which tend to take much longer than non-televised games, it is interesting to see that the rule change alone was able to reduce the game duration back to what it was in the 80s.

I wonder what else has affected the average game duration over the last 40 years. The graph shows other fairly sharp drops and peaks, so I wonder if there were any rule changes or changes in MLB broadcasting that caused those changes in average game duration. I also wonder how players feel about the change, because it likely disrupts their game rhythm and requires them to adapt to a faster pace of play.

This relates to me because I have been a fan of the MLB for a while and I found the games to be slow and at times boring compared to other sports like basketball and football. I hope this change will make baseball more enjoyable to watch with less downtime between pitches.

raw_comment:
There’s a noticeable sudden change in the average game duration after the new rule was implemented, leaving the average game time about 30 minutes shorter than it was last year, which is seen in the yellow segment of the line chart. 
Something I wonder from the visualization is why the average game lengths have increased so much since 1980, since it seems that the average game length has steadily increased since then (with some fluctuations, but the overall trend was increasing). I don’t know if the increase was potentially from other rule changes or just changes in behavior of coaches and players. I also wonder about the effects of this rule change on baseball games. I'm curious not only to how this will affect viewership and game attendance but how this will impact the way the game is played.
This relates to me because I grew up watching MLB games and attending Giants' games. Although I don't watch as many games now I still support the team!
Something I might title this graph is “On the Clock: New MLB Rule Leads to Quicker Games.”

raw_comment:
1.Between the years 2022 and 2023, I noticed a decrease in the typical game duration. In addition, I observed that since 1980, the typical game lasts longer compared with three hours. The mid-2000s saw a modest fall between the peak between the middle of the 1990s and the mid-2010s. Changes to the rules can have been made to shorten this time period as well. The biggest decline occurs between 2022 and 2023, most likely as a result of the pitch time change and the introduction of transmitters for the pitcher and catcher to reduce time spent delaying. I believe that the restriction on infield shifting and the longer bases would lengthen playtime.
2.I'm curious about the data's sample size for 2023. The new restrictions have undoubtedly cut down on the amount of time, but the 2023 baseball season is still in its infancy. With more rivalry games having their games prolonged to earn more income, there can be noticeable variations in the average game length as the season goes on.
3.Stereotypes aside it is critical to understand that i live in a dominican and puerto rican rich community so baseball is important part of the culture in my city. Going to the barber shop all the barbers are placing bets with a each other on whos going to win, but sometimes the games last forever, i feel like this change is so important because it helps increase viewer engagement. 
4.  New baseball rules hit it out the park towards in increase of viewer engagement.

raw_comment:
Interestingly, the average game duration has not been so low since the 1980s, so it would appear the new rules achieved their goal. I find it interesting because I think that baseball was considered more popular and widely enjoyed around that time, so the increasing game duration could be a cause of why baseball has decreased in popularity. I feel like this is the graph that has provided the least information as compared to others in the series. I do appreciate how straightforward it is, though.

I wonder what exactly these new rules are and how thorough they are. Do they specifically reference reducing time through shortening game time, such as lowering points requirements, or do they attempt to reduce time by speeding up game set-up and clean-up? I wonder about the shortest and longest MLB game time ever and the cause.

I am not an avid baseball fan, but I went to a Giants game, which was fun, more so because of the carnival-like atmosphere in the stadium than the game itself. I have a lot of friends and family who enjoy baseball and are pretty big fans, though! I know the length of most sports games can be long, and people often don't go to games unless it is intense or finals of some sort.

My title would be "New Rules in Major League Baseball Result in the Shortest Game Times since the 1980s."

raw_comment:
I noticed that the x-axis has the years from 1980 to 202, with 2022 and 2023 labeled on the graph. The y-axis has the average game duration in hours and minutes. This axis doesn’t start at zero, which can be misleading because it makes each jump look much larger now that they are zoomed in. For instance, the 2022-2023 difference, highlighted in orange looks massive, but it is only a 29-minute difference. There are tick marks on the y-axis for every 15 minutes, and none for the years. The games have steadily increased in duration, with a few decreases once a decade around 1995, 2005, and 2015. 
I wonder what caused the steady increase in game durations since 1980. I also wonder if the longer games impacted the players or the audience. Are they being shortened because people couldn’t sit and watch a three-hour game or were the players getting worn out? As the rest of the season continues, will this pattern of a decrease in duration continue or will it rise back up to three hours? 
I used to watch my local baseball games on TV and remember thinking they were the longest sports match out of any sport. One of my close friends is very involved in baseball and has been talking about the change of rules and the visualization helps to show the difference the new rules are making. 
I would title this: “Major effects of new rules in Major League Baseball”

raw_comment:
Pitch Clocks: Changing the World of Baseball
I notice that in the graph there has been a steady increase of MLB game times from 1980 to 2020. However, in 2022-2023 there is a dramatic decrease. At the height of game times it was at roughly 3 hour and 10 minutes a game and then in 2022 it dropped to 3 hours and 8 minutes and then to a solid 2 hours and 39 minutes in 2023. I wonder why it took the MLB to instill this rule into the games until 2020, if they saw the increase, why did they wait so long? This relates to my community because i’ve gone to various baseball games and MLB games where i’ve recently seen the pitch clock be implemented. Although it does make baseball games shorter, I don’t think i’m rather fond of the pitch clock. It makes the game feel more rushed and there is less control that the players have in the game. In this graph it shows the change in MLB game times in correlation to years from 1980 to 2023.

raw_comment:
1) I notice that there was a significant decrease in time from 2022 to 2023 as it went from 3 hours and 8 minutes to 2 hours and 39 minutes. The last time the game's duration lasted around 2:39 was in the 80s. The year 2020 has the longest timing within the data. Overall, statistically, this graph illustrates a fluctuation as each year has somewhat of a change in the time durations of a baseball game. 

2) The biggest question is why such a sudden change in the duration of games. I wonder since the 1980s had a similar time duration as 2023, how was baseball played at that time? For example, we know 2023 lowered the duration because of new rule changes - what rules did the 1980s have to have baseball games last about 2 hours and 35 min? Moreover, what rules were enforced in baseball games in 2020 that led games to have a duration of 3 hours and 10 minutes? 

3) Since we are in spring and soon to be entering summer, the sport that is very popular in my community is baseball. I've never really been to a game, but from what I've heard and seen from my friends who enjoy baseball, the time of games varies.

"New Rules, Shorter Games, MLB Makes a Change!"

raw_comment:
The first thing that I noticed was the dramatic decrease in the average game duration from 2022 to 2023 which really shows that the implementation of the pitch clock really had an effect on the duration of a game.  Some other things that I noticed are that from around 2000 and 2010, game durations were lower and then started increasing the next decade.  

I don't really watch baseball but the thing that I'm wondering is, if there wasn't a pitch clock before, then theoretically could a baseball pitcher stall the whole game?  Maybe not to the extent of the whole game but for certain periods of time that will tire out the opposing team and make them impatient.  To be honest I'm surprised that no such thing as a clock existed in baseball already.

This relates to my community because I know that baseball is one of those sports that is played a lot recreationally and is played at high levels in high school, college, and beyond.  A new implementation of a pitch clock after all these years seems like a big rule change and can really affect how games are played nowadays.

The Major League Takes A New Step!: The Pitch Clock

raw_comment:
I notice that the graph has had a positive trend upward, indicating longer game times, since 1980. However, with the pitch clock implemented this year, average game times dropped by almost 40 minutes. I wonder why it took so long to come up with a policy to address the problem of games getting continually longer and longer, and also why they increased at the rate that they did. I think that the result of this change makes games more fun to watch and enjoy. Personally, when watching games in past years I felt that they would drag along a lot longer than they needed to, and now that they go by at a quicker pace it's able to hold my attention better than it did before.

raw_comment:
After looking at the average game duration graph, it appears the average game duration has substantially decreased from 3:08 in 2022 to 2:39 in the 2023 season, mainly due to the pitching clock. It also seems that since the 1980s, baseball game lengths have been steadily increasing. 

I wonder if the decrease in-game time impacts the revenue generated by the MLB from advertisements and concession sales. Could the increasing length of the game be due to the rise of TV advertisements? Could shortening the game make advertisers less likely to run ad campaigns through baseball games? I also wonder if changing the base sizes increases the number of hits and runs scored. 

This change relates to my community because I am an avid sports fan and frequently watch MLB games. Since the game times are shorter, I can watch more games, given my busy schedule. It will also increase viewership because people will see more sports action in less time.

Title: The Thinking Sport Picks up the Pace

I also saw that the average time duration had peaked to 3 hours and 8 minutes in the year 2021. Since 1980, the average time has fluctuated steadily and has never remained the same for a year.

I'm wondering as to whether the typical game times will remain at 2 hours and 39 minutes or if they'll change in the coming years. New rules might be added in response to how this affects the games, lengthening the average game time even more. I also wonder what this graph would look like if the entire season's data were used instead of just the first three seasons of the year 

This relates to me because where I'm from people don't usually speak on baseball. In my town people are mostly interested in basketball, soccer, and football. So after seeing this graph, I feel like the MLB should make some changes to its rules which could have a huge positive impact on its publicity

raw_comment:
I noticed a drop in the average game duration between 2022-2023. I also noticed since 1980, the average game duration averages above three hours. Between the highest point between the mid-1990s and the mid-2010s, a slight dip occurs in the mid-2000s. There could have been some rule changes to reduce time in this time period too. 2022-2023 has the steepest drop, most likely due to the pitch time and the pitcher and catcher getting transmitters so there would be less time stalling. I think the ban on infield shifting and larger bases would increase time on the field.

I wonder why and how these changes, especially the pitch clock, are being enforced. Are there penalties for going over the pitch clock? How much time is given to the pitcher's team?

This relates to me because I played baseball when I was younger and I enjoy watching MLB baseball games. I feel that the pitch clock and transmitters reduce the amount of time spent standing on the field. Because playing baseball is a team sport and a lot of time is used to communicate with both teams and all members. When I went to watch baseball games, I remember they took too long and it felt more like waiting for people at bat. With these changes, games will be faster.

"From Slowball to Fastball: How Baseball Games are Speeding Up"

In between the two time periods, there was a fairly strong positive trend of the average duration getting larger, until 2023. 2) I wonder what caused the MLB to implement these new rules. I do feel like more than 3 hours is quite a long time for games, so implementing these rules could make the game more efficient for baseball players and baseball fans alike. 
3) This relates to my community because members of my family are avid baseball fans and probably used to get bored when there were delays in the games, so these new changes may make them more attentive. 
4) "Swing and Shorten: How New Rules are Affecting the Length of MLB Games "

I also noticed that from 1980 to 2022, even though there is a little fluctuation, the average game duration has overall been steadily increasing over the years.

This doesn't relate to me because I am not involved in baseball or the MLB as other people. However, I've gone to some baseball games and it can get a little slow at times but I've enjoyed my time watching these games and never truly minded how long the games lasted.

raw_comment:
I think it’s very interesting that although there are fluctuations in the average game duration, we have overall seen a trend of game time increasing until the introduction of the new rules in 2023. I wonder what caused this increase. It doesn’t surprise me that these new rules led to such a steep decrease right off the bat(some baseball humor), but I do wonder how the introduction of these rules will change game benchmarks like points scored in a game and function of the outfield. Additionally, I think it will be interesting to see how fan viewership, tickets sold, and food sold in the arenas changes. When there is more data I definitely would like to see a graph showing how these aspects of the game changed against average game time.  

Although I don’t know too much about baseball, I have always enjoyed attending Giants games with my family during the summer in San Francisco. I have never really minded the pace of the game, if anything it was a reason to dress up in orange and eat junk food in a stadium full of screaming fans. So it does make me a bit sad to see that they want to reduce the gametime. However, I can see for die hard fans who are very much focused on the play how picking up the pace may be a way to keep them more invested.

I think a good title for this graph could be “The Major League: Pushing Pace for the People”

I also wonder how much these game times vary each year. Have these new rules decreased the variation?

This relates to me because I am a fan of baseball but OI am also a busy college student. Shorter, more fast paced games means that I am able to watch entire baseball games and have more time for my other obligations.

raw_comment:
The first thing that I notice is how drastic a change in the average length of a game has taken after these new rules have been implemented. We can notice that it dropped about 15%. The graph though may be a little misleading as visually it can appear that it is a much larger distance. A drop this size is not irrelevant though.
The first thing that I wonder is how does this change the game. Will people like a faster game? Is this just for profits, or is it for players? Are there any people whom these new rules negatively affect? I feel that strategy will become a lot more important in these games. 
I am not a huge sports fan but I do enjoy going to games with my family. I think increasing the speed of the game will be more exciting but I do not know if that will make it more enjoyable. I recently saw a family friend who said she showed up late to a Dodger game and missed almost half the game.

New Rules on Deck

raw_comment:
One thing that jumped at me was the game duration increase from 1980 to 2022. This is easily noticed in the graph, with the gray time series plot showing a positive sloped trend from 1980 to 2022. This could be contributed to more commericals being aired, and potentially other rule changes that can extend the length of the game.

I wonder what the sample size is for the 2023 data. Sure, there is a noticeable decrease in time that can be attributed to the new rules imposed, but the 2023 baseball season is young. There could be noteworthy changes to the average game duration as the season progresses, with more rivalry matchups having the games extended to generate more revenue.

While I personally am not one to watch baseball, I have a few friends that are highly invested into the league, along with many people within my community. This decrease in watch-time could allow these people to use their time to further explore other facets of the game or use it elsewhere, creating a more efficient system.

A catchy headline could be "Finally, You Can Sit Through a Baseball Game". While this is a bit of a dig at the fans of baseball, the game itself is highly drawn out with minimal action for extended periods of time, making it hard to watch for some relative to other popular sports. So, this title piques the interest of people who do not regularly watch baseball along with the target audience of baseball fans.

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 

I notice that from 1980 to 2022, the average duration of the games gradually increases.  Even though there have been several decreasing trends throughout the years, the overall trend from 1980 to 2022 has been increasing. However, the average duration of the games has decreased exponentially during the 2023 season after several new rules have been enforced. The average duration of the game is three hours and eight minutes for 2022 but it is two hours and thirty-nine minutes for 2023. The average duration of the game for 2023 closely matches the average duration of the game for 1980. 

What do you wonder?

I am interested to know which specific new rule enforced this season has affected the average duration of the games the most. Is the new rule enforcing the pitch clock the main reason why the average duration of the game has decreased for 2023? 

How does this relate to you and your community?

I am a college student and I have several classmates that are currently following several baseball games. Since there are many teenagers and adults that are interested in baseball games, having baseball games that last too long may make them lose interest. One of the main reasons is that many teenagers and adults need to study or work and they could not speed too much time watching baseball games. 

Catchy headline: MLB Has Taken Major Actions to Shorten the Average Duration of Baseball Games.

The main point on the graph is how the time of the baseball games has decreased this past year by nearly 30 minutes. The graph does a great job highlighting this through the use of color. The graph indicates an upward trend in the average game duration from 1980 to 2022, before the new rules led the sharp decline. The game length is now near the times of the 1980s.

This does not relate to me, as I don't care about baseball much. This would be interesting for my sister, who is an avid Padres fan.

I would title this graph "How the MLB Takes Me Out To The Ball Game For A Shorter Time"

raw_comment:
Previously, baseball game durations witnessed regular fluctuations, however there was still a gradual increase in the overall average game duration. However, the 2022-2023 school year experienced a steep decline in average game duration that was almost as low as that of 1980. In those 40 years, there was never a shift that drastic. 

I wonder how closely the rule changes and this decrease in average game duration are related. Were the rule changes purely due to observations by the MLB, or was the MLB experiencing a sharp decline in viewership due to the seemingly never-ending games? Even for those who are not baseball fans, one thing most people are aware of is that baseball games tend to last hours on end. My prediction is that over time, people’s attention spans have gotten too short to sit through entire games. 

Baseball is a very popular sport in America. There are many baseball fans in my own community. The decision may impact this select community positively, as they can watch their favorite teams play without dedicating hours on end to watching games. However, it could also impact them negatively, as there are some baseball fans that enjoy the entire experience and do not want games to feel rushed. My prediction is that ordinary people might become more inclined to start watching baseball, however those who are already baseball fans might not appreciate this new change as much.

raw_comment:
I noticed that the 2023 season (2 hours, 39 minutes) had an average game duration that was 29 minutes shorter than the 2022 season (3 hours, 8 minutes). Looking at the graph, this is the shortest average game duration in the past three decades.

I wonder if the average game durations will stay around the 2 hour 39 minute mark or if they will be shorter or longer in the following years. Depending on how this impacts games, new rules may be added so that the average game duration changes even further. I also wonder how this graph would change if we included data from the whole season rather than just the first three weeks. 

This relates to me because my younger brother loves to watch and play baseball. At this point, my family considers themselves a “Dodgers family”. As much as I love to watch baseball, I think the games can run really long, so shorter games would work in my favor.

This graph shows the average baseball game duration for the first three weeks of each season from 1980 to 2023. I think a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea is  “Let’s Play Some Ball”.

raw_comment:
I noticed that the average game duration was at its highest right before the drop this year. The drop this year is mostly due to the pitch clock, which sets a limit on the time between pitches. I also noticed that average game duration was relatively low around the year 2005 and then spiked up suddenly after that. 
I wonder why the average game duration spiked so quickly after 2005. I’m not aware of any rule changes made during that time so I wonder what factors played into the increase. I also wonder if the MLB will continue to implement changes to make the games go faster or if they are satisfied with the game duration right now.
As someone who watches baseball occasionally, the pitch clock has definitely made a noticeable difference in the pace of the game. Personally, I like the change because I usually don’t have enough time to watch a full baseball game with the previous rules. Now, I find the games to be more enjoyable and faster-paced. 
Fastball!

raw_comment:
I notice that there is a dramatic drop in the average game duration for MLB games from 2022 to 2023. Looking at the graph before 2023, the average game duration was on a rocky but steady increase, having grown from ~2hr 35 mins in 1980 to ~3hr 12mins in 2022. In 2023, the average game length was 2hr 39 mins, nearly back to the average time over 40 years before.

I wonder why the average time increased so much before 2023. The description noted that this dramatic decrease in time is most likely due to the new rules put into place, especially the implication of the pitch clock. There are several other rules added, such as a ban on the infield shift and bigger bases. I wonder how these other changes may have also affected the shortened time.

This does not directly affect me because I would not identify myself as a baseball fan nor do I play baseball, but I have many friends and family members who are and I am sure that these changes and the shorter average duration of a game will change the way they watch and enjoy baseball.

raw_comment:
I noticed a steep drop this year in MLB game lengths from 3:08 in 2022 to 2:39 in 2023. Since MLB implemented a pitch clock to speed up games, this drop in time makes sense. It’s interesting to examine how this trend has fluctuated over the years with game time reaching a high water mark in the early 2010s. Back in the 1980s, however, games were approximately 2.5 hours long - roughly the same as the times this year.

Given that the data was taken through the first three weeks of the season, I wonder if this plot would change if data from entire seasons were used. It’s possible that weather and seasonality might alter these numbers or if players got more used to the new rules changes. 

I’m a baseball fan, so this trend is definitely something I was cognizant of and excited to see. The pace of games are much quicker, more enjoyable to watch, and have increased action on the field. It certainly seems like players have adjusted pretty quickly and the game has improved for the better. 

A potential name for this graph might be “Pace of Play.”

raw_comment:
I noticed that in the past year, the average game length has drastically decreased from 3 hours to 2 hours and 39 minutes. Before 2020, the game duration was steadily increasing with slight drops every few years. I noticed the average game length in the past 40 years from 1980 to 2022 has increased by more than 30 minutes.

Why was the data collected only in the first three weeks of the season? How might this impact the stats? Could this have an effect on the team standings? What caused the game time to go down so much around 2005 - 2006? Why was the game time so short in the 80s? Is there anything besides rule hanges that has caused game time to fluctuate so much? 

Most of our group doesn’t watch baseball because we find it boring. Maybe now that they’re making it more fast paced it will be more appealing to us. The change over in game time might also cause more traffic near the twins stadium. If the game gets out earlier, it might get out closer to busy times downtown. This might get annoying as well.

raw_comment:
1) What do you notice?
I notice that the graph is depicting average game durations from 1980-now, something that has been gradually increasing over time/has a positive trend up until 2023. The peak/maximum was in 2022, an average of 3hr 8mins. Between 2000 and 2010, there was a dip in game durations, the averages reaching a local minimum in 2005 of about 2hr 50mins. However, the minimum of the graph is around 1980 with a time of about 2hr 34min, a time 2023 reached very close to (2hr 39min) after the stark drop in time after 2022's max- the steepest decrease in the graph. 
2) What do you wonder?
I wonder why games suddenly became shorter between 2000 and 2010, and what generally caused games to elongate over time prior to the new 2023 rules.
3) How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because baseball is very big culturally, and the lengths of games- whether too long or too short- effects people's entertainment.
4) What’s going on in this graph?
My headline would be "Does 2023 Mark The End of Long Baseball Games?"

1) The average game time has experienced a positive trend from the 1980s to 2022, but there was a recent decline from three hours and eight minutes in 2022 to two hours and thirty-nine minutes in 2023—a 29-minute decrease. There was also a high of almost three hours in the late 1900s, which could have occurred for a number of lurking variables, such as extra innings from an intense game.

2) I'm curious how the new regulations' adoption will affect MLB viewing. I'm intrigued to see how the new regulations will affect the style of play. I'm also curious about the impact of shorter games on the players themselves, who will have more time to expend their energy.

3) Baseball is frequently disregarded in my home community, owing to its duration in comparison to more "engaging" sports like football or basketball. This adjustment has the potential to make attending the sport more feasible for a far larger number of individuals. As someone who grew up watching baseball, innovations in the sport are both welcome and encouraging, demonstrating that sports continually evolve and are not limited to past traditions.

4) Batter Up! MLB Swings for the Fences With New Rules: Is it a Swing or a Miss?

This one year drop definitely shows that the new rules that were instituted work to speed up games. Maybe this steep drop is due to players not being used to the rules, and the average time will trend upwards again? 
I wonder why games from 1980 to 2022 have been increasing in average game duration at a steady pace. Although there are many peaks and valleys in the game duration, there seems to be an upward trend in the overall average game duration. Personally, I am not really into baseball so I this doesn't really affect me. However, a few of my friends are very into baseball so this will be interesting to see how they react to this news. 
A catchy headline would be: "MLB Rules Speeding up Games"

raw_comment:
I notice that, while the average game duration has been steadily increasing over the years (1980 - 2022), there is a sharp decline in average game duration from 2022 to 2023. 

I wonder if this new rule will get more people watching baseball. Based on what I have read online, this was the main purpose of the additional rule. However, I wonder if there are other factors at play in regards to why people are not watching baseball. I have heard some complaints regarding the availability of baseball on certain streaming networks, and I wonder if this is truly what is decreasing baseball viewership.

Although I personally do not care about baseball or know anyone that cares about baseball, this relates to me and my community because my apartment faces my college's baseball stadium. It is quite loud and frequently wakes me up in the morning on the weekends. And the organ music frequently disturbs my studies. I hope that my school's baseball games also decrease in length, so that I do not have to hear it for as long. 

A new catchy headline could be "Game on! How a New Baseball Rule Shortens Playtime"

raw_comment:
I noticed that there was an increase on times with a couple of dips in the data, the increase on time dropped when these new rules were implemented, now the times for games are more or less equal to the times in 1980, when the data was starting to be taken. The line is yellow is the line after the rule was implemented and it has a steep drop.

I wonder why the game times need to go down, I would think that it would make sense to make the games longer that way you could justify selling tickets at a higher price to fans, but at the same time I suppose that it could lower viewer rates at home. Maybe as a more modernized form of viewing happens we as an audience are more suited to receive clips of games than full length games. 

Baseball is a very prevalent sport for those in my community and a lot of people I've met use it as an escape, my dad and I would watch baseball games when I was younger and it was a good form of bonding. The times being cut down could potentially mean that the networks want a more serialized version of the game where they can't find loopholes in the rules.

"Run! Run! Run around the Diamond: Baseball game durations are cut due to new rules"

raw_comment: I notice that the largest change in average game times was from 2022 to 2023, which is highlighted by the yellow—practically vertical—downward sloping line. The average game duration in the first 3 weeks of the 2022 MLB season was 3:08, and this year it drastically decreased to a game duration of 2:39 hours on average in the first 3 weeks of the season. I wonder why game durations began to mostly increase from 1980 to 2022, and how the changes in the MLB’s rules have contributed to the overall increasing trend for most of the graph. I also wonder if game durations are related to the overall evolution of baseball players since the 1980s, since sportsmen and women have generally improved over time with new technologies, strategies, and training regimens. This relates to me because I have seen this graph a few weeks ago in one of my college Statistics courses, where we had a discussion as to why there appears to be a significant decrease in the average MLB game duration from 2022 to 2023: the MLB officially implemented a new pitch timer rule which limits the time that pitchers have to pitch the ball to 15 seconds when there aren’t men on bases and 20 if there are. I wonder how this new rule will impact the viewership rates for baseball. I personally have never gotten into baseball because the sport felt too long and slow and I know many of my friends feel the same way.

raw_comment:
1) I notice that from 2022 to 2023, game duration has decreased by 29 minutes on average, from 3:08 to 2:39. At the same time, average game duration in 1980 also appears to be about 2:39, meaning in the last 43 years, there has been almost no net change in average game duration.

2) I wonder if the average length of the games, which was increasing from 1980 to 2022, was affected by level of competition. Hypothetically, players were the best they have ever been in 2022, as new training techniques would allow massive gains in skill level.

3) This relates to me and my community because being from San Diego, many of my peers are Padres fans. For the more casual fans such as myself, games can stretch to an undesirable length, so these changes make the game more accessible.

4) There is a plot comparing year against average game duration, where it is seen to be staggered yet increasing from 1980 to 2022, then a large downturn in 2023. There are a few local maximums throughout since the increase was not constant.

1.) What I noticed is that the amount of time an average game took to play in the MLB from 2022-23. It's interesting how low the average game time dropped to, almost as low as it was in 1980. This is likely due to the new pitch clock mentioned, that places a time limit on how long a pitcher can take to throw. 
2.) I wonder why this drop is incredibly significant. I thought that the game time would decrease with a timed pitch clock, but I had no idea by that much. I think maybe pitchers now have to worry about pitching within the given time slot, and now make their throws much earlier than they normally would, even if there is still a lot of time on the pitch clock. They might feel that pressure of being on a time limit, and pitch earlier than they normally would. But I wonder if this is truly the case for most pitchers now, or just some of them.
3.) I think this graph relates to my community because if pitching has now gotten its own time limit at the major league level, maybe soon this will become an implementation at all levels of baseball, even at the college level with my friends who do baseball. they might also have to worry about pitching sooner than they normally would, and it could mess up their focus.

raw_comment:
Generally speaking, I like the display of this graph. It is simple, yet still communicates the intended message very clearly. The axis labels are in large enough font to easily follow, the lack of color makes the intended numbers stand out. The data-ink ratio is carried out very well. There are no unnecessary words, figures, etc., the axis values are consistent, and the two labeled data points clearly depict a drastic change in game time for M.L.B. games. I do think it will be interesting to see how this new rule change will affect the popularity of the sport. I think it will increase the popularity. Given that baseball games do not consist of constant action, a shorter game might keep fans more engaged. 
Before this year I did not know much about baseball at all, but I have attended a couple of my university’s games this season and my only complaint about the sport is how long the games are. I love the environment of a baseball stadium and the excitement of the crowd, but three hours of baseball is far too much for me. I am more than supportive of the pitch clock if that means a slightly shorter game. 
A catchy headline for this graph could be, “Baseball: America’s Pastime is Catching up to Speed”

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that for the year 2023, the duration time hit its ultimate steepest and most drastic decrease. The difference is 29 minutes of reduction. I also noticed that around the year 2021, the average time duration had also hit its peak. The average time has consistently been changing since 1980 and has not been consistent for any year.
2. I wonder if the new rules were not implemented, would in future years the average time duration surpasses the 3 hr 15 min mark? I wonder if the baseball fans had anything to do with the change since they might have felt that a 3 hour game is a very long time. I also wonder what caused the 3 hour peak in the year 1995 since the averages of the other years were way lower. 
3. This relates to me and my community because my family loves to watch baseball but at home. The games are too long and most of us don't like being in one place for multiple hours. At home, watching the games on tv, we can do other things while the game is on but no one really sits and watches for the entire game time. If the average game time keeps reducing, we would probably go watch a game in person since it won't be as long.
4. Hit The Winning Home Run Before The Time Strikes You Out

raw_comment:
The first thing I noticed, probably like most people, is the major decrease in the amount of time an average baseball game lasts from 2022 to 2023. The average game duration is almost the lowest it has ever been. This change is a direct effect of the new pitch clock that was implemented into the game, a rule that I personally think was great for the game. 

One thing I wonder is will we continue to see the same pitch clock moving forward, a new modified pitch clock, or will they get rid of it all together? I hope that they continue to grow of the current pitch clock and make it better.

This relates to me and my community because I am an athlete who grew up playing baseball along with other sports. My dad is a huge Red Sox's fan so I am as well. Although I don't really watch the MLB, I have kept up with the season to see how the new pitch clocks plays out.
